strings.name: Richard Flanagan
strings.role: Novelist · Nonfiction writer and film director
strings.summary: Flanagan began in nonfiction before drawing Tasmania's history, families and rivers into novels. The Narrow Road to the Deep North explores war, love and trauma through prisoners of war and won the Booker Prize. Question 7 joined family memory and global history, winning a nonfiction prize. His writing also addresses ecology and the responsibilities of literary sponsorship.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Writes war memory, family and ecology in works including The Narrow Road to the Deep North, extending Australian literature internationally.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Longford, Tasmania, Australia; grew up in Rosebery.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Arts degree at the University of Tasmania; Rhodes scholar at Worcester College, Oxford, earning a history MLitt.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Fiction and war memory
strings.highlights.h1.text: The Narrow Road to the Deep North explores violence, love and survival through railway prisoners of war.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Between fiction and memoir
strings.highlights.h2.text: Question 7 links family, the atomic age and a near-death experience in nonfiction.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Published Heresies
strings.timeline.t1.text: Collected about two decades of essays, articles and speeches on ecology, democracy, family and literature.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Won a nonfiction prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: Question 7 won the Baillie Gifford Prize; he delayed accepting money over the sponsor's fossil-fuel investments.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published an ecological family novel
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Living Sea of Waking Dreams juxtaposed a mother's dying with Australian fires.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Won the Booker Prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Narrow Road to the Deep North won the annual fiction award, widening his international readership.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Published Gould's Book of Fish
strings.timeline.t5.text: Reimagined colonial Tasmania through a convict painter; won the Commonwealth Writers' Prize the next year.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Published an immigrant-family novel
strings.timeline.t6.text: The Sound of One Hand Clapping portrays Slovenian immigrants; he later directed its film adaptation.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First novel published
strings.timeline.t7.text: Death of a River Guide follows personal and family history through a drowning man's memories.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Received a Rhodes scholarship
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from study in Tasmania into historical research at Oxford.
